ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF DONGGALA REGENCY
NUMBER 5 OF 2014
CONCERNING
PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and regional governments currently places very great attention on the existence of children. Based on their existence as the nation's future generation who are qualified and dignified, the government and regional governments are obligated to recognize the existence of children's rights in their humanity. The human rights inherent in children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. In supporting the realization of children to grow and develop, children need various adequate educational facilities and infrastructure, development of talents and interests. In order to realize the right to protection and the right to participation, children need serious attention from various parties, both government, regional government and society.
Specifically regarding protection efforts from violence that threatens the safety and health of children and women must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or other people. For women and children experiencing these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget, the role of various parties to help handle violence problems faced by women and children include social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious figures.
The condition of children's deterioration along with their rights and the condition of violence against women and children that frequently occurs in the region should become a common concern for all stakeholders without exception, including regional governments to play a role in preventing and overcoming such deterioration and violence.
For the regional government of Donggala Regency in facing the universe of conditions above, various actions are taken to fulfill children's rights as well as: prevent and assist in handling acts of violence against women and children which are endeavored by establishing a Regional Regulation concerning Protection for Women and Children.

CHAPTER V
HANDLING OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST
WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Article 20
(1) Regional governments are obligated to prepare medical personnel at community health centers (Puskesmas) or hospitals specifically to handle victims. (2) Medical personnel as referred to in paragraph (1) are obligated to provide complete health services to victims.

Article 9
(1) Regional governments provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb through community health centers and hospitals.
(2) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.
(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) are provided free of charge for families who are unable or poor families.
(4) Regional governments implement activities to support the provision of breast milk to infants.

Article 21
Regional governments are obligated to assist in providing adequate special rooms for victims at Resort Police Agencies (Polres) and at every Sector Police agency.
Article 22 (1) Social workers or volunteer personnel as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) letter b are tasked with accompanying victims in facing the process of resolving acts of violence.
(2) Social workers or volunteer personnel in addition to being tasked as referred to in paragraph (1) carry out activities including:
a. counseling or guidance to strengthen and provide a sense of security for victims;
b. providing information regarding the rights of victims to obtain protection from the police and the establishment of protection orders from the court;
c. escorting victims to safe houses or alternative residences; and d. conducting integrated coordination in providing services to victims with agencies or related parties needed by victims.

Article 23
(1) Regional governments are obligated to prepare Safe Houses to be used in temporary handling for victims of violence against women and children.
(2) Safe Houses as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be provided in every Sub-district.

CHAPTER VI
FINANCING
Article 26
(1) The costs of activities related to the implementation of protection for women and children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget as well as other lawful revenues in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Activity expenditures sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget shall be budgeted in the Regional Work Unit that handles the affairs of implementing protection for women and children in accordance with the needs and financial capacity of the Region.
(3) The budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1) must be budgeted by the Regent and DPRD and determined every fiscal year in the APBD.

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) The construction of Safe Houses is prioritized within the vicinity of every Sub-District Office.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article I
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Bupati is the Bupati of Donggala.
2. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of Donggala Regency as an element of regional government administration.
3. Regional Government is the Bupati of Donggala and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus work unit of Donggala Regency that handles the interests of women and children.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the apparatus work unit located within the SKPD of Donggala Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb and a person recognized by law.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law.
8. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all actions and services to fulfill rights, as well as to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence.
10. Child protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Referral is an effort referred to protect victims of violence.
12. Violence is any act against a person, especially women and children, that results in or may result in physical, sexual, psychological misery and suffering, neglect, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
13. Physical violence is an act that results in pain, injury, or causes misery, including miscarriage or unconsciousness.
14. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness or severe psychological suffering in a person.
15. Sexual violence is the coercion of sexual relations, coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
16. Victim of acts of violence hereinafter referred to as victim is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or economic loss, emotional, deprivation of fundamental rights as a result of an act of violation of human rights (HAM), or criminal acts and acts of violence that occur both by state apparatus or by regional government apparatus or by other persons.
17. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
18. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Institution is a non-governmental organization (NGO) that conducts assistance.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of women and/or children.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Supervision is the activity of observing, listening, examining, reviewing, assessing the implementation of protection of women and children.

Article I
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

ON

NUMBER 5 OF 2014
CONCERNING
PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and regional governments currently places very great attention on the existence of children. Based on their existence as the nation's future generation who are qualified and dignified, the government and regional governments are obligated to recognize the existence of children's rights in their humanity. The human rights inherent in children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. In supporting the realization of children to grow and develop, children need various adequate educational facilities and infrastructure, development of talents and interests. In order to realize the right to protection and the right to participation, children need serious attention from various parties, both government, regional government and society.
Specifically regarding protection efforts from violence that threatens the safety and health of children and women must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or other people. For women and children experiencing these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget, the role of various parties to help handle violence problems faced by women and children include social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious figures.
The condition of children's deterioration along with their rights and the condition of violence against women and children that frequently occurs in the region should become a common concern for all stakeholders without exception, including regional governments to play a role in preventing and overcoming such deterioration and violence.
For the regional government of Donggala Regency in facing the universe of conditions above, various actions are taken to fulfill children's rights as well as: prevent and assist in handling acts of violence against women and children which are endeavored by establishing a Regional Regulation concerning Protection for Women and Children.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF DONGGALA REGENCY
NUMBER 5 OF 2014
CONCERNING
PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and regional governments currently places very great attention on the existence of children. Based on their existence as the nation's future generation who are qualified and dignified, the government and regional governments are obligated to recognize the existence of children's rights in their humanity. The human rights inherent in children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. In supporting the realization of children to grow and develop, children need various adequate educational facilities and infrastructure, development of talents and interests. In order to realize the right to protection and the right to participation, children need serious attention from various parties, both government, regional government and society.
Specifically regarding protection efforts from violence that threatens the safety and health of children and women must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or other people. For women and children experiencing these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget, the role of various parties to help handle violence problems faced by women and children include social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious figures.
The condition of children's deterioration along with their rights and the condition of violence against women and children that frequently occurs in the region should become a common concern for all stakeholders without exception, including regional governments to play a role in preventing and overcoming such deterioration and violence.
For the regional government of Donggala Regency in facing the universe of conditions above, various actions are taken to fulfill children's rights as well as: prevent and assist in handling acts of violence against women and children which are endeavored by establishing a Regional Regulation concerning Protection for Women and Children.

13. Physical violence is an act that results in pain, injury, or causes misery, including miscarriage or unconsciousness.
14. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness or severe psychological suffering in a person.
15. Sexual violence is the coercion of sexual relations, coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
16. Victim of acts of violence hereinafter referred to as victim is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or economic loss, emotional, deprivation of fundamental rights as a result of an act of violation of human rights (HAM), or criminal acts and acts of violence that occur both by state apparatus or by regional government apparatus or by other persons.
17. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
18. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Institution is a non-governmental organization (NGO) that conducts assistance.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of women and/or children.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Supervision is the activity of observing, listening, examining, reviewing, assessing the implementation of protection of women and children.

Article 21
Regional governments are obligated to assist in providing adequate special rooms for victims at Resort Police Agencies (Polres) and at every Sector Police agency.
Article 22 (1) Social workers or volunteer personnel as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) letter b are tasked with accompanying victims in facing the process of resolving acts of violence.
(2) Social workers or volunteer personnel in addition to being tasked as referred to in paragraph (1) carry out activities including:
a. counseling or guidance to strengthen and provide a sense of security for victims;
b. providing information regarding the rights of victims to obtain protection from the police and the establishment of protection orders from the court;
c. escorting victims to safe houses or alternative residences; and d. conducting integrated coordination in providing services to victims with agencies or related parties needed by victims.

NUMBER 5 OF 2014
CONCERNING
PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and regional governments currently places very great attention on the existence of children. Based on their existence as the nation's future generation who are qualified and dignified, the government and regional governments are obligated to recognize the existence of children's rights in their humanity. The human rights inherent in children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. In supporting the realization of children to grow and develop, children need various adequate educational facilities and infrastructure, development of talents and interests. In order to realize the right to protection and the right to participation, children need serious attention from various parties, both government, regional government and society.
Specifically regarding protection efforts from violence that threatens the safety and health of children and women must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or other people. For women and children experiencing these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget, the role of various parties to help handle violence problems faced by women and children include social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious figures.
The condition of children's deterioration along with their rights and the condition of violence against women and children that frequently occurs in the region should become a common concern for all stakeholders without exception, including regional governments to play a role in preventing and overcoming such deterioration and violence.
For the regional government of Donggala Regency in facing the universe of conditions above, various actions are taken to fulfill children's rights as well as: prevent and assist in handling acts of violence against women and children which are endeavored by establishing a Regional Regulation concerning Protection for Women and Children.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and regional governments currently places very great attention on the existence of children. Based on their existence as the nation's future generation who are qualified and dignified, the government and regional governments are obligated to recognize the existence of children's rights in their humanity. The human rights inherent in children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. In supporting the realization of children to grow and develop, children need various adequate educational facilities and infrastructure, development of talents and interests. In order to realize the right to protection and the right to participation, children need serious attention from various parties, both government, regional government and society.
Specifically regarding protection efforts from violence that threatens the safety and health of children and women must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or other people. For women and children experiencing these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget, the role of various parties to help handle violence problems faced by women and children include social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious figures.
The condition of children's deterioration along with their rights and the condition of violence against women and children that frequently occurs in the region should become a common concern for all stakeholders without exception, including regional governments to play a role in preventing and overcoming such deterioration and violence.
For the regional government of Donggala Regency in facing the universe of conditions above, various actions are taken to fulfill children's rights as well as: prevent and assist in handling acts of violence against women and children which are endeavored by establishing a Regional Regulation concerning Protection for Women and Children.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF DONGGALA REGENCY
NUMBER 5 OF 2014
CONCERNING
PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and regional governments currently places very great attention on the existence of children. Based on their existence as the nation's future generation who are qualified and dignified, the government and regional governments are obligated to recognize the existence of children's rights in their humanity. The human rights inherent in children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. In supporting the realization of children to grow and develop, children need various adequate educational facilities and infrastructure, development of talents and interests. In order to realize the right to protection and the right to participation, children need serious attention from various parties, both government, regional government and society.
Specifically regarding protection efforts from violence that threatens the safety and health of children and women must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or other people. For women and children experiencing these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget, the role of various parties to help handle violence problems faced by women and children include social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious figures.
The condition of children's deterioration along with their rights and the condition of violence against women and children that frequently occurs in the region should become a common concern for all stakeholders without exception, including regional governments to play a role in preventing and overcoming such deterioration and violence.
For the regional government of Donggala Regency in facing the universe of conditions above, various actions are taken to fulfill children's rights as well as: prevent and assist in handling acts of violence against women and children which are endeavored by establishing a Regional Regulation concerning Protection for Women and Children.

ON

NUMBER 5 OF 2014
CONCERNING
PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and regional governments currently places very great attention on the existence of children. Based on their existence as the nation's future generation who are qualified and dignified, the government and regional governments are obligated to recognize the existence of children's rights in their humanity. The human rights inherent in children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. In supporting the realization of children to grow and develop, children need various adequate educational facilities and infrastructure, development of talents and interests. In order to realize the right to protection and the right to participation, children need serious attention from various parties, both government, regional government and society.
Specifically regarding protection efforts from violence that threatens the safety and health of children and women must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and maltreatment by parents or other people. For women and children experiencing these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget, the role of various parties to help handle violence problems faced by women and children include social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious figures.
The condition of children's deterioration along with their rights and the condition of violence against women and children that frequently occurs in the region should become a common concern for all stakeholders without exception, including regional governments to play a role in preventing and overcoming such deterioration and violence.
For the regional government of Donggala Regency in facing the universe of conditions above, various actions are taken to fulfill children's rights as well as: prevent and assist in handling acts of violence against women and children which are endeavored by establishing a Regional Regulation concerning Protection for Women and Children.

For women and children experiencing these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget, the role of various parties to help handle violence problems faced by women and children include social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious figures.
The condition of children's deterioration along with their rights and the condition of violence against women and children that frequently occurs in the region should become a common concern for all stakeholders without exception, including regional governments to play a role in preventing and overcoming such deterioration and violence.
For the regional government of Donggala Regency in facing the universe of conditions above, various actions are taken to fulfill children's rights as well as: prevent and assist in handling acts of violence against women and children which are endeavored by establishing a Regional Regulation concerning Protection for Women and Children.

6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb and a person recognized by law.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law.
8. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all actions and services to fulfill rights, as well as to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence.
10. Child protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Referral is an effort referred to protect victims of violence.
12. Violence is any act against a person, especially women and children, that results in or may result in physical, sexual, psychological misery and suffering, neglect, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
13. Physical violence is an act that results in pain, injury, or causes misery, including miscarriage or unconsciousness.
14. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness or severe psychological suffering in a person.
15. Sexual violence is the coercion of sexual relations, coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
16. Victim of acts of violence hereinafter referred to as victim is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or economic loss, emotional, deprivation of fundamental rights as a result of an act of violation of human rights (HAM), or criminal acts and acts of violence that occur both by state apparatus or by regional government apparatus or by other persons.
17. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
18. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Institution is a non-governmental organization (NGO) that conducts assistance.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of women and/or children.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Supervision is the activity of observing, listening, examining, reviewing, assessing the implementation of protection of women and children.

4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus work unit of Donggala Regency that handles the interests of women and children.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the apparatus work unit located within the SKPD of Donggala Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb and a person recognized by law.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law.
8. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all actions and services to fulfill rights, as well as to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence.
10. Child protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Referral is an effort referred to protect victims of violence.
12. Violence is any act against a person, especially women and children, that results in or may result in physical, sexual, psychological misery and suffering, neglect, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
13. Physical violence is an act that results in pain, injury, or causes misery, including miscarriage or unconsciousness.
14. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness or severe psychological suffering in a person.
15. Sexual violence is the coercion of sexual relations, coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
16. Victim of acts of violence hereinafter referred to as victim is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or economic loss, emotional, deprivation of fundamental rights as a result of an act of violation of human rights (HAM), or criminal acts and acts of violence that occur both by state apparatus or by regional government apparatus or by other persons.
17. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
18. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Institution is a non-governmental organization (NGO) that conducts assistance.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of women and/or children.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Supervision is the activity of observing, listening, examining, reviewing, assessing the implementation of protection of women and children.

CHAPTER VI
FINANCING
Article 26
(1) The costs of activities related to the implementation of protection for women and children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget as well as other lawful revenues in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Activity expenditures sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget shall be budgeted in the Regional Work Unit that handles the affairs of implementing protection for women and children in accordance with the needs and financial capacity of the Region.
(3) The budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1) must be budgeted by the Regent and DPRD and determined every fiscal year in the APBD.
